Inclusion is the generic term; reinforcement is the subset where continuous stress transfer occurs MSE wall: near-vertical reinforced fill structure; RSS: reinforced slope with face < 70 degrees Facing plays a minor structural role — primarily prevents raveling between reinforcement layers Reinforced fill and retained backfill are distinct zones with different material requirements

figures.caption: Representative MSE applications (a) retaining wall; (b) access ramp; (c) waterfront structure; and (d) bridge abutment. 2-2
figures.description: Applications Selection of MSE wall or RSS for transportation retaining structures and slope stabilization. MSE walls cost-effective alternative to RC/gravity walls for abutments, wing walls, restricted ROW Cost savings >50% over conventional walls on poor foundation sites (eliminates pile foundations) Temporary MSE walls widely used for detours, temporary abutments, phased construction RSS: face inclination < 70 degrees; two purposes: (1) increased slope stability, (2) improved edge compaction RSS can reuse slide debris rather than importing higher quality fill RSS with nonwoven geotextiles provides in-plane drainage for pore pressure dissipation in cohesive fills

figures.caption: Cost evaluation of reinforced soil slopes. 2-10
figures.description: Relative Costs Preliminary cost comparison between MSE walls, RSS, and conventional retaining structures. MSE walls typically 25-50% less expensive than conventional RC retaining structures Permanent MSE walls: $30-65/ft2 ($320-650/m2) face area — varies widely by region and fill cost Reinforced fill (select granular) is typically 30-60% of total MSE wall cost MBW faced walls < 15 ft (4.5 m) typically 10% or more less expensive than segmental panel walls RSS costs $10-24/ft2 ($110-260/m2) depending on height; reinforcement is 45-65% of cost Small projects < 3,000 ft2 (300 m2): unit cost 10-15% higher than larger projects

figures.caption: Erection of precast panels. 2-21
figures.description: Construction Sequence Construction of MSE walls and RSS for both precast panel and flexible-faced systems. Leveling pad: unreinforced concrete, ~1 ft wide x 6 in. thick; not a structural foundation, only a guide Loose lift thickness maximum 12 in. (300 mm); compact to 95-100% AASHTO T-99, dry of optimum Reinforcements placed perpendicular to wall face; connected when fill reaches connection level Only first tier of precast panels requires bracing; subsequent rows wedged/clamped to adjacent panels Hand compactor required within 3 ft (~1 m) of wall face to avoid panel displacement Flexible face: minimum 4 ft (1.25 m) return fold for pullout resistance; adjacent sheets overlap min 6 in.

figures.caption: Potential external failure mechanisms for a MSE wall 4-18
figures.description: Step 6 – Evaluate External Stability External stability checks for all routine MSE wall designs. Four external failure modes: sliding, eccentricity, bearing, global stability Table 4-5 resistance factors: bearing 0.65, sliding 1.0, global stability 0.65-0.75 Wall facing weight and width neglected in all external stability calculations Sliding and eccentricity use minimum EV + maximum EH load factors

figures.caption: Calculation of eccentricity and vertical stress for bearing check, for horizontal backslope with traffic surcharge condition 4-24
figures.description: Step 6b – Eccentricity Limit Check Eccentricity (overturning) check at base of MSE wall for Strength I limit state. e = eccentricity = distance between resultant load and L/2 Soil foundations: e ≤ L/4 (resultant within middle half of base) Rock foundations: e ≤ 3L/8 (resultant within middle three-quarters of base) Use min EV + max EH; live load excluded from stabilizing side Increase L if eccentricity criterion not met Step 6c – Evaluate Bearing on Foundation Foundation bearing resistance check for all MSE walls (Strength I and Service I). Bearing eccentricity eB uses max EV + max EH (different from eccentricity check which uses min EV) Live load included in bearing check (applied over full reinforced and retained zone) Factored bearing pressure σv = V / (L - 2eB) — Meyerhof uniform
